summary: Created opsbot on both nodes. A node-generated ED25519 key on node1 now provides opsbot access to node2. Both SSH servers require public-key authentication for opsbot. Configuration and access persisted through sequential node restarts.
actions_performed: Created opsbot accounts with home directories on node1 and node2.
Generated the private key on node1 and installed only its public key on node2.
Configured both SSH servers to require publickey and disable password and keyboard-interactive authentication for opsbot.
Verified node1-to-node2 command execution as opsbot and explicit password-only rejection on both systems.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, confirmed changed boot IDs, and reverified service, configuration, key data, and access recovery.

evidence.requirement: opsbot accounts and SSH key installation
evidence.summary: opsbot exists on both nodes; node1 owns the private key and node2 has the matching authorized key with restrictive permissions.
Effective SSH configuration requires publickey and disables password and keyboard-interactive methods; password-only attempts were rejected by both nodes.

evidence.requirement: opsbot can run commands on node2 from node1
evidence.summary: Successful sessions identified the remote user as opsbot on node2 before and after both restarts.
Baseline boot ID 55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358 changed to 5662c915-6c42-42e4-a225-9307d74a859e; sshd, opsbot, key data, policy, and remote access recovered.
Baseline boot ID 31949c21-52ad-47af-bdbe-893352fd509b changed to 10b0e0cd-9936-4187-a474-3f2363ab62a9; sshd, opsbot, authorized key, public-key-only policy, and end-to-end access recovered.
